Subject: Recap + proposed benchmark sweep (latency & throughput)

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and a suggested plan for the competitive benchmark sweep you asked for: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary workload: near-real-time product search/assist in web UI (avg prompt ~120 tokens, tail queries up to 2k tokens).
- SLAs you care about: interactive feel for users (p95 target ~250ms, p99 as low as possible ideally <500ms), and throughput to support 500 concurrent users / ~250 tokens/sec sustained per instance.
- Procurement/legal will want SOC2 + standard SSO + data retention terms.

Proposed benchmark sweep (high level)
1) Short context, cold cache: 120-token prompts, single-request latency distribution (p50/p95/p99).
2) Long context, warm KV cache: 2k token prompts with KV cache warm; measure p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
3) Throughput ramp (tokens/sec): measure tokens/sec at concurrency 50/200/500, including batching heuristics.
4) A/B: Redwood runtime vs Hyperscaler API (you mentioned Azure + one other). We'll run identical request traces.

What we need from you
- A sample set of 50 representative prompts (CSV is easiest) OR permission to use anonymized request logs.
- Confirmation of the two hyperscaler endpoints you want included (Azure and GCP?) or a specific vendor report (attach if available).

Attachments: sample_prompts.csv, mutual_action_plan.docx (stubbed)

Timing: we can run an initial sweep next week (Mon/Tue) if we get the prompts by Friday. I'll loop in Marissa with the detailed config.

Next steps proposed (simple bullets)
- You send sample prompts or logs.
- We schedule a 2-hour bench window and share results + p95/p99/tokens-per-second matrix.
- Procurement: we’ll provide SOC2 evidence and a short statement of data flows.

If this looks good I’ll lock a slot and share the bench plan + config.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

On Wed, Mar 17, 2026 at 15:02, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.inference> wrote:
> Quick recap... proposed plan...

Thanks — looping in the engineering bench team. Below is a compact bench config we recommend and a set of Redwood internal baselines run on the same model family (7B-class quantized) to set expectations. These are internal numbers on a single A100-equivalent instance with our runtime optimizations enabled.

Recommended sweep config (details attached in bench_config.yaml):
- Model variant: redwood-l1-7b-quant (closest open analog to what we demoed)
- Sequence lengths: 120 (short), 512 (mid), 2000 (long)
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 16 (to measure batching benefits)
- Concurrency: 50, 200, 500 (simulated users)
- Cache states: cold (fresh process), warm (single-session KV warm), persistent cache (prefix reuse)
- Measurement: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec (aggregate), GPU tokens/sec (per-GPU), 99.9th CPU spike events

Redwood internal baseline (single-instance, warm cache, 120-token prompts):
- p50: 58 ms
- p95: 180 ms
- p99: 420 ms
- sustained tokens/sec: 320 tokens/sec
- cost estimate: ~$0.0018 / 1k tokens (engine-only estimate)

Hyperscaler sample (published / comparable run we have for same trace):
- p50: 95 ms
- p95: 260 ms
- p99: 780 ms
- sustained tokens/sec: 190 tokens/sec

Notes and caveats:
- We tune batching aggressiveness to avoid 99.9 spikes — there’s a tradeoff between p95 and tokens/sec.
- Long-context runs (2k tokens) increase p95/p99 significantly; we plan to capture latency vs cost curves.
- We can provide raw CSVs of the full distributions and an html dashboard after runs.

Attachments: bench_config.yaml (run parameters)

Marissa
